title: Solo dev, grand strategy game of antiquity (509 BC – AD 476) – how AI brought me back to game dev after decades
author: AOM_Dev
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev,

I'm the solo developer of **Age of Mankind**, a grand strategy game set between 509 BC and AD 476. The world map stretches from the edge of Spain to Japan and has about 9,000 provinces.

You can play any of several hundred historical peoples, from Rome and Carthage to Han China, either in free play or in one of the historical scenarios. Peoples change their names over time depending on the date and how big they have grown. The AI plays by the same rules as the player and can build its own empire. Everything runs in real time on one big map. More core mechanics and 3D battles are in development right now. The trailer shows the current build, where battles are still resolved automatically.

Now to the part that fits this sub: AI... and why do I use AI at all? Simple. Without AI I could never pull off something like this on my own.

Many years ago... actually it's been a few decades now 😃 ...I hung around in the modding communities of certain games and worked on mods myself. The problem was always the same: everyone's time. When a mod dragged on for a long time, people dropped out. It got really bad when one or more programmers left the boat. Then the project was basically dead. After that happened a few times, and because working life caught up with me too, I stopped modding.

Now, decades later, AI came along, and at first I was a total opponent like many others: "Nobody needs it, it's overrated, it's useless, you only make crap games with it, it's just hype." But after reading more and more reports over months about where AI is used and what's possible, curiosity got me. So I tried different coding AIs, ended up sticking with Claude, and I have to say... "breathtaking"! :)

**So which AI tools do I actually use, and for what?**

\* Claude: helps me with the code, and it's also where I collect all my ideas, because it organizes them really well.

\* ElevenLabs: music and sounds. I'm not fully convinced by the sounds yet, music works better. The song in the trailer, for example, is from ElevenLabs.



If you have any questions about the game or how I use AI, just ask here. Anyone else who came back to game dev because of AI?

And if you like what you see, a wishlist or a subscription helps a lot ❤️😄

comments.author: Ouvolk
comments.body: I think you should at least name the games it is inspired from. Looking at the visuals and the title, it seems to me that it is  inspired from either Imperator: Rome or EU5

replies.author: AOM_Dev
replies.body: Hi Ouvolk, it is more inspired by CK3, because I love that game. Unfortunately you can't control your armies in battle there, and for my taste the game covers too few years. That's why Age of Mankind runs for almost 1,000 years, and 3D battles you can command yourself are what I'm working on right now.
